item.content:encoded: The University of West Florida Argos suffered a lopsided 35-7 loss to Abilene Christian on Saturday night in their latest test competing at the Division I FCS level. Despite entering the game ranked No. 17 nationally, UWF couldn't overcome a dominant first half by the Wildcats, who built a four-touchdown lead by halftime and cruised to victory at Wildcat Stadium. The result underscores the growing competitive challenge facing the Argos as they continue their transition into FCS football. Abilene Christian, a two-time United Athletic Conference champion, improved on its 1-4 season record with the dominant performance.

item.title: North Escambia veterans gain weekly in-person service office hours in Century

item.content:encoded:
Military veterans and their families in North Escambia now have regular access to local assistance without traveling far from home. National Veteran Service Officer Tim Chandler will hold weekly office hours every Tuesday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Century Chamber of Commerce building, 7811 North Century Boulevard, beginning this week.

The move brings veteran services directly to the northern part of Escambia County, making it easier for local veterans to access support with benefits, claims, and other services in person. Chandler's office will operate consistently on Tuesdays, providing a predictable schedule for veterans seeking assistance.

item.title: Escambia County Rehabs Fishing Pier at Lake Stone in Century

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Parks and Recreation is moving forward with a routine maintenance project at Lake Stone in Century, replacing aging wooden piers and railings to keep the popular fishing destination safe and functional.

The pier has been temporarily closed while crews handle the rehabilitation work. Lake Stone Campground, situated at 801 West Highway 4, spans 100 acres and serves the community as both a campground and boat ramp facility, making the pier a key amenity for anglers and water enthusiasts in North Escambia.

County Parks and Recreation did not specify a timeline for completion of the project or when the pier would reopen to the public.

item.content:encoded: A Century-based youth organization is asking the Escambia Children's Trust for more than $1 million to expand early childhood learning and family readiness services in northern Escambia County. Extra Mile Club Str8 Up will present its proposal to the Escambia Children's Trust Program Committee during a regular meeting scheduled for Tuesday, October 6. The organization says the funding would support expanded services aimed at preparing young children and families in the area. The committee will consider the request as part of its regular agenda.

item.title: TSA PreCheck Members Can Now Visit Gates at Pensacola Airport Without Flying
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola International Airport has launched a new program that lets approved visitors accompany passengers to the gate area—no plane ticket required. The initiative, called Gateside by TSA PreCheck, allows people with active TSA PreCheck memberships to clear security checkpoint screening without a boarding pass, according to reporting from North…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport has launched a new program that lets approved visitors accompany passengers to the gate area—no plane ticket required. The initiative, called Gateside by TSA PreCheck, allows people with active TSA PreCheck memberships to clear security checkpoint screening without a boarding pass, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The program is designed to give families and friends more time together before departure, eliminating the need for visitors to watch travelers disappear through the security line. It's a convenience feature that several major U.S. airports already offer, and now travelers using Pensacola International can take advantage of the same benefit.

To participate, visitors must have an active TSA PreCheck membership and go through the standard security screening process at the airport. The program applies to the gate areas but does not permit access to other restricted airport zones.

item.content:encoded:
The entire Pensacola area is under a flash flood watch through Sunday evening as multiple rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected throughout the weekend. Forecasters warn that heavy rainfall could lead to flash flooding in the region.

Saturday's forecast calls for a chance of showers and thunderstorms in the morning, becoming more likely after 10 a.m., with highs near 83 degrees. The wet pattern is expected to continue through Sunday evening, with additional rounds of storms possible.

Residents and drivers are urged to be cautious, particularly in flood-prone areas and along roadways. Stay weather-aware and avoid driving through standing water, as conditions could change rapidly throughout the weekend.

item.title: Escambia County Commission meetings scheduled Oct. 5–9
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County government has a busy week of public meetings and hearings lined up from Monday through Thursday, with a full roster of planning, development, and administrative sessions. Monday morning, the county will hold an IAFF Demand to Bargain session at 9 a.m. at the Public Safety building on North W Street. Tuesday features back-to-back…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County government has a busy week of public meetings and hearings lined up from Monday through Thursday, with a full roster of planning, development, and administrative sessions.

Monday morning, the county will hold an IAFF Demand to Bargain session at 9 a.m. at the Public Safety building on North W Street. Tuesday features back-to-back Planning Board meetings starting at 8:30 a.m., along with hearings on affordable housing, environmental enforcement, and the Children's Trust Program. The FloridaWest Economic Development Alliance Finance Committee will also convene Tuesday afternoon.

Wednesday's schedule includes the Bellview East Neighborhood Cleanup at 7 a.m., followed by meetings of the Contractor Competency Board, Development Review Committee, and the Local Mitigation Strategy group. Thursday wraps the week with a FloridaWest Executive Committee meeting at 8:30 a.m. Friday has no meetings scheduled.

Most sessions are held at the Escambia County Central Office Complex at 3363 W. Park Place unless otherwise noted. Residents can watch proceedings live or on-demand via MyEscambia.com/ectv, YouTube, or local cable channels. Those needing accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act should contact Human Resources at 850-595-3279.

item.title: USPS releases 2026 Christmas stamp featuring 16th-century Madonna and Child painting
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service unveiled its 2026 Christmas stamp Thursday, featuring a richly detailed 16th-century painting titled "The Virgin and Child Enthroned" from the collection of the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown, Massachusetts. The oil-on-panel work, painted around 1500, depicts Mary in elaborate red garments trimmed…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service unveiled its 2026 Christmas stamp Thursday, featuring a richly detailed 16th-century painting titled "The Virgin and Child Enthroned" from the collection of the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown, Massachusetts.

The oil-on-panel work, painted around 1500, depicts Mary in elaborate red garments trimmed with gold and jewels, holding the Christ child dressed in white. According to the USPS, the painting is distinctive for its intricate background details — including angels, a glimpse of a Dutch city, and what art historians interpret as the heavenly Jerusalem — alongside carefully rendered Christian symbols. A dog represents faith, pomegranates suggest fertility and resurrection, and strawberries symbolize righteousness.

Greg Breeding, an art director for USPS, said the painting's "beautiful red folds" and "ornate patterns" caught his eye, along with its unusually detailed composition compared to other Madonna and Child depictions. The stamp continues a tradition dating to 1966, when the first Madonna and Child Christmas stamp was issued. The Postal Service printed 185 million copies as Forever stamps, meaning they will always equal the current First-Class Mail rate for one ounce.

item.title: Pensacola seeks community input on Fricker Center playground redesign
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The city opened a public poll Friday that runs through October 23, inviting the community to vote on two design concepts: Red, White and Blue, or Teal and Green. Residents can access the…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola is asking residents to weigh in on plans for a new playground at the Fricker Resource Center as renovation work continues at the facility. The city opened a public poll Friday that runs through October 23, inviting the community to vote on two design concepts: Red, White and Blue, or Teal and Green.

Residents can access the poll on the Fricker Center project website, where they'll find detailed renderings of both playground options. The survey asks voters to select their preferred design and layout, indicate which ADA-accessible features matter most to them, and offer general feedback on the proposals.

The Fricker Resource Center serves as a community hub in Pensacola, and the playground renovation is part of a larger facility improvement initiative. City officials are encouraging families and neighbors to participate in the voting process to ensure the final design reflects what the community wants to see.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

Robinson, who represents House District 71, is an attorney specializing in real estate, land use, and local government law at Blalock…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis has appointed State Representative Will Robinson to the State College of Florida, Manatee-Sarasota District Board of Trustees, according to an announcement from the governor's office Friday.

Robinson, who represents House District 71, is an attorney specializing in real estate, land use, and local government law at Blalock Walters, P.A. He previously served on the Judicial Nominating Commission for Florida's Twelfth Judicial Circuit and chaired the board of Meals on Wheels PLUS of Manatee. Robinson holds a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Notre Dame and a law degree from Stetson University College of Law.

The appointment requires confirmation by the Florida Senate.
